result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would make it so that every human being could truly understand—at a gut level, not just intellectually—what it is like to be another person: to feel their specific fears, their quiet hopes, the weight of their history, the texture of their loneliness or their joy.

Not to force agreement or erase difference, but to make cruelty impossible to sustain. To make indifference feel, for once, physically uncomfortable. To let someone look at a stranger and recognize them as a self as real and intricate as their own.

I think most of the harm we do to each other comes from a failure of imagination, not a surplus of evil. We protect our own tribe because the other tribe is abstract. We hoard because we cannot feel the hunger we are not experiencing. We wound because we have never really felt the wound we are inflicting.

If that barrier dissolved—if empathy became as involuntary as breathing—the architecture of the world would have to change. Not through policy or revolution, but because you could no longer build a world that hurt people without feeling the hurt yourself.

That, I think, is the change I would make.
